consensus_summary: Nine weakness sub-claims are carried in immutable EIC→R1→R2→R3→DA source order through six non-ranking REV items. REV-02 joins the compatible but distinct SC-02 and SC-05 response surfaces; REV-04 joins the distinct SC-04, SC-06, and DA-M1/SC-08 scope surfaces while preserving each source's severity, anchor, and confidence. No weakness reaches CONSENSUS-3 or CONSENSUS-4, no non-DA weakness is explicitly disputed, and the DA CRITICAL table is empty. The residual candidate remains (A0_WEAK_ARITHMETIC_RELATION,A1_FAIL,A2_FAIL,A3_FAIL,A4_FAIL) / ROUTE_A_REJECTED; the homology calibrator remains (A0_FAIL,A1_PASS_ANALYTIC,A2_FAIL,A3_FAIL,A4_FAIL) / ROUTE_A_REJECTED; Q_11 is a separate changed-owner/tower/clock/normalization fixed-finite-panel control that cannot rescue the residual candidate; Route B remains unavailable.
dissenting_opinions: R1 passes D3 because the theorem and certificate chain is internally coherent, while DA warns D3 because headline necessity language is broader than the registered intervention class; the D3 F3 majority predicate remains false at 1/2.

EIC and R2 regard the bounded factorial specialization, compact-versus-cusped comparison, owner firewall, and quadrant audit as defensible local contributions, while DA-M2 requires a precise theorem-level increment or consistent comparative-methods/calibration positioning.
